sentences.text: Poundland has collapsed into administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk, after its owners failed to find a buyer to keep it in business.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: The discount retailer formally entered administration on Wednesday afternoon, just weeks before Christmas.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: Poundland's American owners held talks with several bidders over a last-minute rescue deal for the business, but no transaction was reached.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: This led to Poundland's boss filing for administration, with consultancy Alix Partners appointed to oversee the process.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: Alix Partners will pursue a sale of the business and its assets, with Poundland likely to be broken up, for example with some of its stores sold off to rival retailers.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: Poundland is facing collapse - what's gone wrong?
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: Previously US-based owner Gordon Brothers was criticised over how it had handled the Poundland sale process, with insiders saying it was driving a viable business into the ground to make money through insolvency.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: But the investment firm, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, had denied the claim.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: Gordon Brothers had stated Poundland was "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading".
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: But this was in stark contrast to Poundland's boss Barry Williams, who had said the business was making a "strong recovery".
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: One of the central stumbling blocks in negotiations to keep the business afloat was a shareholder loan Gordon Brothers inherited when it bought the business for less than £1 last year.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: Gordon Brothers was owed £22.5m of that loan, while the previous owner Pepco was owed £7.5m.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: Gordon Brothers rejected various offers to buy the business as a going concern with deals to pay off that loan.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: Irish firm Martin Property Group offered to pay off £5m of the loan up front, and defer the rest of the payments to 2030.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: Gordon Brothers also rejected a deal from the London-based Xyra group, which offered £12.5m up front but ran out of time to get a deal over the line.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: A German investment firm, Zachert Private Equity, is also understood to have made a late offer, but that too was rejected.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: The crisis at Poundland really came to a head over the past few weeks after Gordon Brothers restricted access to some funds for day-to-day operations.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: This meant that stock at the retailer was not being replenished at the necessary pace in the vital run-up to the festive period.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: On the funding question, Gordon Brothers said it had put £85m into the firm over a year to help save it from insolvency.
sentences.article_title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Moment Raheem Sterling arrested after car crash Former England footballer Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended sentence after admitting dangerously driving his Lamborghini while inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon on a motorway.
sentences.article_title: Raheem Sterling given suspended jail sentence for dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession

sentences.text: The 31-year-old, from Berkshire, who later crashed into a metal gate during rush hour,  gave no reaction as he was handed a 12-month jail term, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court.
sentences.article_title: Raheem Sterling given suspended jail sentence for dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession

sentences.text: Sterling had pleaded guilty to dangerous driving of a Lamborghini Urus and possessing nitrous oxide on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road on 28 May.
sentences.article_title: Raheem Sterling given suspended jail sentence for dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession

sentences.text: The judge said Sterling's use of the Class C drug had became a "maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period"  in his career.
sentences.article_title: Raheem Sterling given suspended jail sentence for dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession

sentences.text: Sterling, who left the court without making any comment, was ordered to complete 100 hours unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.

sentences.text: He was arrested after crashing near the M3 in Hampshire.
sentences.article_title: Raheem Sterling given suspended jail sentence for dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession

sentences.text: Raheem Sterling - from national icon to suspended jail sentence District judge Kirsty Allman told the court on Wednesday that Sterling was seen at 01:10 BST at a McDonald's in Hayes driving "erratically and at speed" while inhaling from a pink balloon.
sentences.article_title: Raheem Sterling given suspended jail sentence for dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession

sentences.text: During the September hearing, prosecutor Simon Jones said a number of calls were made between 07:45 and 08:52 BST about a black sports car and the manner it was being driven.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Footage was released of the footballer driving dangerously Witness Christopher Jennings called 999 after driving alongside Sterling's car on the M25, and "he was shocked by what he saw", Jones said, and made clear "he sighted the defendant inhaling from the balloon".

sentences.text: Fiona Jennings – driving on the southbound M3 – described the driving as "absolutely horrendous" and "swerving in and out of lanes", the court heard.

sentences.text: The court heard Sterling strayed into the central reservation of the M3, exited at junction 4A, and veered off the A327, crashing into a metal gate near a layby.

sentences.text: His vehicle sustained "substantial damage to the tyres and bodywork and was no longer capable of being driven", the court heard.

sentences.text: Sterling was taken to Basingstoke police investigation centre by officers, where he disclosed he had a "problem with nitrous oxide", said Jones.

sentences.text: The substance is legally sold for catering, medical and industrial purposes but is frequently used as a recreational drug, commonly known as laughing gas.

sentences.text: Defending Sterling on Wednesday, Jason Bartfeld KC said there was no dispute that this was a "top category case" because of prolonged driving and "at times" serious impairment which would have been short periods within the driving.

sentences.text: The AI promise (left) did not match the reality (right) The organisers of a Christmas market have cancelled all bookings and promised to refund stallholders following a backlash to AI-generated promotional materials.

sentences.text: President Cyril Ramaphosa has faced calls to resign over his handling of the "Farmgate" scandal South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has won a legal battle to overturn a report that found he may have a case to answer over the theft of large sums of cash from his private farm.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: In 2022, an independent panel said Ramaphosa may have committed serious misconduct relating to the theft of $580,000 (£443,000), hidden in a sofa, at his Phala Phala game farm in the Limpopo province.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: He denied any wrongdoing.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: Ramaphosa challenged the findings of the report in court after the Constitutional Court ruled that parliament had violated the constitution by blocking moves to impeach him.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: The Western Cape high court ruled that the panel's report was unlawful and set it aside "in its entirety".
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: In its judgment, the court said the panel, appointed by parliament to investigate the allegations against Ramaphosa, had "misconstrued its function, the nature of the inquiry it was to conduct and the recommendation it was required to make".
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: "It went beyond its lawful remit ... and made several material errors of law. [Therefore] the report of the independent panel ... is declared unlawful and is reviewed and set aside in its entirety," Judge Nolwazi Mabindla-Boqwana said.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: The court also declared unlawful the steps taken by parliament in relation to the report.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: Political analyst Khanyi Magubane said the court ruling was a victory for Ramaphosa as it gave him "political and constitutional credibility".
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: She made it clear that the ruling was not a criminal finding on possible improper conduct at the farm but rather an indictment at the independent panel's report.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: "[So] he does get significant reprieve ... but there will always be the shadow of the Phala Phala report," Magubane said.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: The ruling effectively removes the basis for the parliamentary impeachment process against Ramaphosa, although opposition parties have indicated they intend to challenge the decision.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: The scandal, dubbed "Farmgate" by local media, has has dogged Ramaphosa since it emerged in 2022, when former spy chief Arthur Fraser reported the matter to police in a dossier.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: Fraser, an ally of former President Jacob Zuma, accused Ramaphosa of concealing the theft from the police and tax authorities.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: The break-in took place in 2020, when thieves allegedly stole bundles of US dollar bills hidden inside a sofa at the farm.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: Opposition parties, pictured above, have been vocal in their call for the president to account for his role in the saga Earlier this month, two people were found guilty of the theft.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: Ramaphosa confirmed that a robbery had taken place but said the money had been from the legitimate sale of buffalo from his livestock business.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: Several investigations cleared him of any wrongdoing, but parliament began an impeachment proceedings in 2022 and appointed an independent panel to investigate the allegations.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: The panel made a series of damaging findings, including that there was "substantial doubt about the legitimacy of the source of the currency that was stolen".
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: It also concluded that Ramaphosa "has a case to answer".
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: Ramaphosa initially challenged the report in court but withdrew his application after parliament voted against adopting its findings.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: He revived the legal challenge again in May this year after the Constitutional Court, the country's highest court , ruled that parliament had acted unconstitutionally by blocking moves to impeach him.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: It ordered parliament to refer the report to an impeachment committee.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: In his latest challenge, Ramaphosa argued that the panel had "misconceived its mandate, misjudged the information placed before it and misinterpreted the four charges advanced against me".
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: The Western Cape High Court's ruling could bring the current impeachment process to an end, unless parliament successfully challenges the decision.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: If they do, and the appeal is successful, the parliamentary committee would be able to examine the charges against the president and make a recommendation.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: If the committee recommends impeachment, parliament would have to vote on whether to remove him from office.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: This would require the support of at least two-thirds majority in parliament.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: Ramaphosa's Africa National Congress (ANC) has enough parliamentary seats to block such a move.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: He is the first president to face impeachment proceedings under the rules introduced in 2018.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: Legal expert Professor Richard Calland told the BBC he had expected the court ruling, given what he termed as "fault lines" in the independent panel's report.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: Calland said the court's findings now meant that the impeachment process was "dead in the water [and] cannot continue".
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: He said that any political party that wanted to revive it "would have to come up with a whole new basis" for this.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: Calland said political parties who want to hold Ramaphosa accountable would likely seek to appeal the ruling but it was unlikely parliament would also do so.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.text: "So, the president's political career is now free of the cloud of impeachment," he said.
sentences.article_title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat

sentences.article_title: Trump's rescue of Nvidia's Huang brings political risks

sentences.text: In the weeks since concerns over Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy first surfaced, Nvidia's stock price tumbled more than 32%.
sentences.article_title: Trump's rescue of Nvidia's Huang brings political risks

sentences.text: Last Friday alone, it fell 14%.
sentences.article_title: Trump's rescue of Nvidia's Huang brings political risks

sentences.text: US stock indices tumbled as well, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq down 10% last week and the larger S&P 500 dropping 8.6%.
sentences.article_title: Trump's rescue of Nvidia's Huang brings political risks

sentences.text: The recent financial turmoil may have given Trump a glimpse into a future where AI growth is just the latest financial bubble – like the housing market in 2008 and internet companies in 2001 – that is due for a resounding pop, with similarly dire economic consequences to follow.
sentences.article_title: Trump's rescue of Nvidia's Huang brings political risks

sentences.text: Trump's intervention on behalf of Huang arrested that drop, at least for a day.
sentences.article_title: Trump's rescue of Nvidia's Huang brings political risks

sentences.text: On Tuesday, Nvidia's stock price gave back much of the bounce it had enjoyed, and larger stock indices were mixed.
sentences.article_title: Trump's rescue of Nvidia's Huang brings political risks

sentences.text: The fate of the America economy and the AI juggernaut that has powered it is still undetermined.
sentences.article_title: Trump's rescue of Nvidia's Huang brings political risks

sentences.text: Trump's intervention may not be a crisis fully averted, but only a crisis delayed.
sentences.article_title: Trump's rescue of Nvidia's Huang brings political risks

sentences.text: And if an AI reckoning does come, the US president will be hard-pressed to avoid being caught in the maelstrom.

sentences.text: Taiwan's ruling party is being repeatedly targeted with AI videos spreading false claims about its leader and other key members ahead of crucial local elections, BBC Verify has found.
sentences.article_title: Is China behind a wave of AI fake videos targeting Taiwan?

sentences.text: A China-linked network has pumped out more than 500 fake videos about the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) in the past year, which experts suggest is part of a long-running campaign to influence the outcome of the elections.

sentences.text: The videos appear to try to smear President Lai Ching-te by claiming he holds a US green card - and would abandon Taiwan if war broke out with China - which Taiwan's presidential office says is completely false.

sentences.text: Bills are set to rise for millions of households, after Ofgem announced that the energy price cap will rise by 26%  in January.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: The main reason for the increase is international gas prices, Ofgem says, but UK energy prices - particularly for electricity - have been high for some time.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Here are three key reasons why that is.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: The price energy suppliers pay for electricity is often determined by a bidding process, with each generating company saying what it would be willing to accept to produce one unit of electricity.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Once built, the cost of generating power from renewables like wind and solar is relatively low, so these typically come in with the cheapest bid.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Gas generators often have high costs because they have to buy fuel to generate electricity as well as paying a "carbon price" - a charge for emissions.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: The wholesale market price is set by the most expensive unit of electricity needed to meet demand.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: This means that even if gas only generates a small proportion of electricity at a given time it can set the overall market price.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: So when gas costs spike - as has happened following the wars in Ukraine and Iran - electricity prices do too.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Not all electricity generation is directly priced in this way.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: For example, newer wind and solar farms are typically guaranteed a fixed price, irrespective of the wholesale price, while some generators enter into direct contracts with suppliers.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: In the first quarter of 2027, the contribution of wholesale energy costs to a typical annual household bill in Great Britain will be £1,216 - up from £604 in the first quarter of 2026 and up from £373 in the winter of 2019-20.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: These figures account for both electricity and gas.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Northern Ireland operates on a separate system to the rest of the UK, being part of the Single Electricity Market with the Republic of Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Analysts say that one of the reasons why energy prices are relatively high in the UK is because of the country's reliance on natural gas - leaving households exposed to gas price spikes.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: While renewables are generating more electricity than a decade ago, a relatively high share still comes from natural gas.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: In 2025 31% of the UK's electricity was produced in that way.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: This compares with just 3% in France, which generated the majority of its electricity - 69% - from nuclear power.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: The US has a higher share of natural gas in its electricity generation mix than the UK - 40% - but American wholesale gas prices are considerably lower thanks to the shale gas production boom of the past 20 years.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Most UK homes also rely on gas for heating, for example, so are directly hit when gas prices rise - as well as those who use electricity.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Another reason energy bills have risen in recent years is down to the cost of expanding and modernising the UK's energy networks.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Those investments are partly to upgrade an ageing gas grid but also to accommodate new wind and solar farms and transmit their power to homes and businesses.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: The network costs contribution to a typical annual energy bill will be £417 in the first quarter of 2027, an increase of £197 from £220 in the winter of 2019-20.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: "We've probably underinvested in the last decade and now we're trying to catch up so there's quite a lot of spending," says Frankie Mayo, an energy analyst from Ember Energy.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: There are other costs associated with renewable electricity.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Many older projects are paid a subsidy on top of the wholesale electricity price - which forms part of policy costs.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: This was designed to encourage investment at a time when renewables were particularly expensive.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Many of these projects are still under contract and so still receive the subsidy, although the government has moved much of these costs off bills and onto general taxation.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: However the government and some energy groups argue that reducing our national reliance on volatile international gas prices via the government's clean power push will keep down the UK's wholesale electricity costs and mean household bills will be lower than they would otherwise have been.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: This would be by reducing the amount of time in each year that gas sets the wholesale electricity price.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: A great deal though depends on future wholesale gas prices which are impossible to accurately forecast.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: Some analysts, including the government's Climate Change Committee, also say the government should go further to remove policy costs from household electricity bills and meet them through general taxation instead.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: That would encourage people to use cleaner electricity rather than gas to heat their homes, they argue.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: "The way you allocate those costs matters," says Mayo.
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: "They may be being put on bills or they may be being paid by consumers in other ways that are less visible, such as taxes."
sentences.article_title: Three reasons why your energy bill is so high

sentences.text: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges On Christmas Eve 2021, there was a knock on the door of Lexi Levens' rented flat.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: It was a letter sent by special delivery from the NHS nurse's landlord saying she, her husband, and four children had two months to move out.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: "The kids all thought it was a present arriving," she recalls.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Lexi's landlord had used something known then as a Section 21 notice to evict her family without needing to give a reason.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Lexi, along with the housing charity Shelter, went on to lobby the government to improve rights for renters.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: The Renters' Rights Act, which came into force in May this year, banned Section 21 evictions and also made it illegal to refuse to rent to people based on their status as a family with children.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: The landlords Lexi had been renting from at that time were typical of the English housing market - individuals who owned one or a handful of properties.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Lexi Levens received a letter on Christmas Eve 2021 telling her that her family had to move out Many of these small landlords say the Renters' Rights Act has left them feeling squeezed.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: They also say rising interest rates, new regulations and tax changes (including some in the most recent Budget) are making things harder.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Some say they are selling up.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Meanwhile, according to Savills estate agents, 2026 is likely to be another record year for investment from large institutions in what is known in the property industry as build to rent (BTR).
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: This is when big developers build blocks of flats or family housing to rent out, something that is commonplace in parts of Europe and the US.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: It means that rather than dealing with an individual landlord or letting agent, tenants are instead renting from larger, typically corporate, entities.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: So does the shift, as some believe, represent a welcome professionalisation of the UK rental sector?
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Or will renters increasingly miss the positive elements of the personal touch that small landlords can provide?
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: According to the latest government survey of private landlords in England, 83% of English landlords own four properties or fewer, representing 51% of tenancies.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: And according to 2024 research by real estate agency Savills, around 40% rental homes in the US and Germany are owned by large institutions - be they private firms, listed companies, pension funds, or co-operatives.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: For the UK, Savills calculated that figure was just 3%.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: But the rental market is changing.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Lexi is pleased with the idea of a sector with stricter rules for landlords and more professional institutions getting involved.

sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Lucian Cook, head of residential research at Savills, says it's not a matter of looking at one policy, government, or council in particular but more the "policy environment" which has been around since the 2010s.

sentences.text: He points to a series of tax changes, including mortgage interest tax relief changes and higher stamp duty rates for second homes and buy-to-let properties introduced by the Conservatives around 10 years ago, which made the sector less favourable for smaller landlords.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: The Renters' Rights Act and more stringent energy efficiency requirements were later introduced.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: And the last two Budgets have raised taxes on rental income from next year.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: The tax change applies to individuals who are landlords, not to BTR companies which pay corporation tax, further encouraging professionalisation of the sector.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Yet, while many welcome these changes, others say they are pushing smaller landlords out of the sector.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: As Cook puts it, there has been more "stick" for small landlords than "carrot" for the BTR sector.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Between 2000 and 2016, a net 2.74 million homes were added to the English rental market in total, according to an analysis of government data by the Joseph Rowntree Foundation.

sentences.text: In the 10 years since, a net of just 200,000 have.

sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Many experts, landlord groups, and tenant groups agree that building more housing - whether that's rental housing or housing for sale - would help solve many of the issues in the rental sector.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: The thinking goes that building more homes for rent, provided people can afford them, would help deal with the supply crunch that can drive up rental costs and force tenants into lower quality properties.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: And building more homes for sale, provided people can afford them, would remove those from the market who don't want to rent but are forced into it.

sentences.text: Kevin Barber resents what he sees as the clout of the BTR sector.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: But whether we will actually see more homes being built is another matter.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Savills' Cook says BTR development could slow in future as high interest rates and increased building costs continue to hit developers' bottom line.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: These same factors are why housebuilders say they are building less.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: Cook says the current rate of BTR development won't be enough to meet the demand for rental properties on its own, at least not imminently.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: In addition, while some BTR developers do build cheaper family homes for rent in the suburbs, the sector is largely still building blocks of flats for wealthier renters living in cities.
sentences.article_title: The shake-up facing renters as a new kind of landlord emerges

sentences.text: This raises the possibility that the UK could end up with a two-tier rental market – what Cook describes as the "haves and the have nots" – where high-earning city-dwelling renters have their pick of rental properties but poorer renters in suburbs struggle to find somewhere to live.

sentences.text: Nvidia and its co-founder Jensen Huang have been at the centre of the artificial intelligence (AI) spending boom.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: No company or chief executive has arguably been more consequential to the development of AI in recent years, with the US microchip manufacturer under Huang positioning itself as a critical cog in the development of the world-changing technology.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: That central position prompted questions, in the aftermath of Huang's departure over revelations of extramarital affairs, over how important he was to the wider AI industry and US economy.

sentences.text: The fact he has been handed his job back after just 11 days in a U-turn by Nvidia's board implies the top brass believe Huang is irreplaceable.

sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: The billions of dollars being funnelled into AI and the construction of data centres has bolstered the American economy, with Nvidia being one of the biggest spenders.

sentences.text: Originally focusing on chips which process graphics for computer games, it pivoted to making the chips used in AI systems and now dominates the market.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: It is now one the most valuable firms in the world and its rapid growth is poised to continue as the firm's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Huang played a major role in the company, leading its shift towards AI, and maintained a firm grip on it, with up to 200 people directly reporting to him.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Some suggested his departure, which was sparked by the emergence that Huang had an affair with a woman alleged to have been a spy for China, posed a risk to the wider AI industry.

sentences.text: That was because it was unclear whether Nvidia would change strategy and potentially rein in spending - a move could have had wider implications for the US economy, but which looks unlikely now Huang has returned.

sentences.text: The fears were sparked due to Nvidia being a key source of finance for many firms, as well as being a microchip supplier.
sentences.article_title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

sentences.text: Sophie Hope's credit score was hit by identity fraud Getting approval for a mortgage, a car loan or even a mobile phone contract can rest on a credit score.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Sophie Hope was on the sharp end of just such a decision.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "When I first checked my credit score, it was excellent.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But then my mortgage application was suddenly denied by the lender because of my credit report.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It was a massive shock as I'd never had bad credit.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: When I looked into it, my score had gone to 'very poor'," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It turns out, the Brighton-based nail technician and content creator, had been the victim of identity fraud.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Someone had opened accounts in my name across various catalogue sites and ordered multiple items, including a PlayStation 4 and Nike socks," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Without me knowing, the debt was transferred to a secondary finance company.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It spent three to four years accumulating in the background.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It was only when I went to apply for a mortgage that I discovered how severely it had dragged down my credit score," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Credit scores are "backward looking" says Funmi Olufunwa Hope's experience shows how crucial a credit score can be, but, as in her case, it does not tell the full story.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "As a nation, we are overly obsessed with credit scores," says Funmi Olufunwa, a consumer finance lawyer and founder of financial education business, Hoops Finance.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Three firms - Experian, Equifax and TransUnion - produce credit scores in the UK, and they all work from roughly the same data.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "A credit score is backward looking.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It's looking at what has happened in the past, which doesn't necessarily predict the future," says Olufunwa.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "But when somebody's looking to lend you money, they're looking at what actually is affordable," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Traditional credit scoring systems also disadvantage "thin-file applicants" - young people and recent immigrants to the UK who won't have built up a credit history.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But with more financial data available than ever before - and a growing appetite for AI to make sense of it - could artificial intelligence help lenders work out who is safe to lend to?
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: In the US lending decisions will often hinge on a credit score from a company called FICO, which uses data from the big three credit assessment firms.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But AI-powered lending firms, Upstart and Zest AI have both built businesses which offer lenders an extra option when it comes to assessing a client's credit worthiness.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Thanks to our machine-learning models that look at more than 2,500 variables, we believe we can make significantly more loans at low prices to borrowers from every demographic group," Upstart said in statement.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But like with many other applications of AI into everyday life, there are concerns.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Consumers need to understand what information is being used to make decisions about them, and they need to be able to challenge something when it is wrong," Tucker explains.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Credit scores have been a contentious topic for decades for this very reason, says Sandra Wachter, professor of Technology and Regulation at the University of Oxford.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "We are not assessing if past decisions were right," Wachter argues, adding, AI does not know about existing social inequalities that impact decisions and could just "replicate what it has seen in the past".
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: While companies like Upstart and Zest AI see technology as a tool for financial inclusion, Wachter believes that real transformation requires accountability, as well as automation.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: She stresses that firms must apply existing regulations and establish new guardrails to ensure that AI does not simply perpetuate the biases of the past.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Not putting any safeguards in place will fortify, foster, and enhance discrimination." Upstart says it is tackling that issue.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "We've invested in creating objective, automated evaluations to identify bias, and we've incorporated those evaluations into our model training process so it evolves to become even more accurate and more fair over time," the company said in a statement.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Evangeline Atkinson (left) and Laura Mills co-founders of Noggin HQ Evangeline Atkinson had a frustrating experience over her credit score.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "I was at university, paying rent, paying bills, as I had been doing for many years.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: No record could be found for me at any of the big three credit reference agencies." That experience inspired her to try to change the system.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: In 2021, Atkinson founded a credit reference agency with her best-friend from school, who had also experienced difficulties getting credit.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Atkinson explains it was set up to help consumers access affordable credit by analysing their current account transactional data.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "You have to be very careful", she warns.

sentences.text: "It's very sensitive data and it would be very easy for the models to be inferring various kind of protected characteristics." sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: As for the future of credit scoring, companies are starting to look beyond traditional methods, according to consumer finance lawyer Funmi Olufunwa.

sentences.text: "They are beginning to realise that traditional credit scoring is inherently backward-looking, and that there are better predictors of the future out there." Whether consumers will be happy with AI playing a part in working out their future credit ratings is another thing.

sentences.text: Photonic chips use light instead of electrons to process data "Photonic chips are on the verge of a breakthrough," says Ton van Mol of the Dutch research institute TNO.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: If van Mol is right – and TNO, the European Union and the Dutch government are backing the idea with millions of euros - then the technology could be a gamechanger.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The chips which run today's society, from your phone and TV, to the vast data centres meeting our insatiable desire for AI, are mostly electrical.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: They process data by shunting electrons around tiny circuits – a single microchip produced today can contain billions of transistors, and sizes are measured in nanometres (one nanometre is a billionth of a metre).
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Because they use light instead of electricity, photonic chips are faster, use less energy and generate less heat than traditional computer chips.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Van Mol hopes for an acceleration in photonics similar to the one seen in electrical chips since the 1970s.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "With optical chips, you are now where electronic chips were maybe 40 [or] 50 years ago." American, Taiwanese and Chinese firms dominate the computer chip industry, but Europe sees the emergence of photonic chips as a fresh opportunity to lead, on what could be, a key future technology.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Which is why the European Union has committed €400m ($450m; £330m) to a project called PIX Europe , external , with the stated goal of making the continent "a global leader in emerging technology for Photonic Integrated Chips".
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe said 'we need to have our own manufacturing in-house'," says van Mol, who is leading a key part of the programme.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Factories with machines that can handle bigger wafers can churn out chips more efficiently.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "[Photonic chip] manufacturing worldwide is [currently] done on wafers which are four inches (10cm) in size, and the next step is to scale-up production to a six-inch wafer," says van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: His team are already building a 10,000 sq m factory to produce six-inch indium phosphide wafers on the High Tech Campus in the Dutch city of Eindhoven.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's due to fully open in 2030 and will be a major step forward, not just for photonics in Europe, but around the world, according to van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "That's the development TNO is going to do, in a pilot line which is really serious.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The Netherlands-based tech giant is the only company in the world able to build the machines needed to make the most sophisticated semiconductors.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Which is why ASML products will sit at the heart of the pilot line in Eindhoven - it's no coincidence that van Mol's project is based around the corner from ASML's headquarters.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "The way you produce these [photonic] chips is very similar to the way you produce electrical or electronic chip," says van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "You use the same type of equipment, you also need a high-end clean room, you also use wafers, so the production method is very similar to the traditional semiconductor technology." ASML itself is keen to explore the opportunities that the emerging technology of photonics could offer.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe has a strong position in photonics research.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The next challenge is translating those innovations into industrial-scale manufacturing," says Stanislas Baron, who is the head of ASML's EU/US Customer Team.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The Eindhoven project has the backing of former ASML chief executive Peter Wennink, author of an influential report for the Dutch government called The Roadmap to Future Prosperity , external , which noted that the market for photonics was expected to grow 10 to 20 times in the next 10 years.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: In a news release backing the new pilot line, Wennink described it as "a launchpad for Europe's future digital economy".
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "By investing in scalable production capacity, we are creating an ecosystem that can help shape the global technological direction," he said.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Of course, Europe is not alone in looking to the potential of photonics to earn a global economic advantage.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: In June this year, US photonics company Coherent announced what it called "the world's first and largest volume-production six-inch indium phosphide manufacturing platform" at its plant in Sherman, in Texas.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The expansion is backed by chip manufacturing giant Nvidia , external , as well as $50 million public funds under the US Chips Act.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's an illustration of how quickly the market is moving, and how central photonic chips could be to the continuing race to retain an influential stake in AI and technological development more generally.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Europe's bid to establish itself as a global leader in photonic chips – exemplified by the Eindhoven project – is the kind of strategy that makes sense in a globalised economy, says Joris Teer, policy analyst at the European Institute for Security Studies in Brussels.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: If the continent can take a lead in photonic chips, then future developments in AI and data will partly be dependent on Europe.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe knows that its high energy and labour costs, skilled workforce shortages, and lack of private and public capital make an across-the-board reindustrialisation strategy impossible", Teer says.

sentences.text: Managing AI agents is a big part of Lotte Underwood's job Recent university graduate Lotte Underwood is a public relations executive with a twist - she spends more time using AI than actually doing PR.

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: The main disability benefit in England and Wales should be more closely linked to the additional costs claimants face, a government-commissioned review has recommended.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The review on personal independence payment (Pip) led by Disability Minister Sir Stephen Timms said the current system was "not appropriate" for claimants who do not have any extra costs arising from their condition.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The government has committed to some of its recommendations, including fast-track payments for people with severe conditions, but will not respond fully to the plans until early next year.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The Conservatives said the year-long review was a "compete farce" and showed a "complete absence of substance".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately added: "All we have is a report that tinkers around the edges of a failed system".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Pip is available to people with long-term physical or mental health conditions who have difficulty doing every day tasks, regardless of whether they work, and it is not linked to income or savings.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The number of people claiming Pip in England and Wales has roughly doubled since 2019 to around four million.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The Timms review was set up last year by Sir Keir Starmer's government after his aborted attempt to cut welfare spending, which was derailed by the threat of a rebellion by Labour MPs.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: It was co-produced with groups representing disabled people, who had a role in drafting the report.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit Giving a statement in the House of Commons, Sir Stephen said Pip "remains a vital source of support" but the system was "no longer fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: He told MPs the current assessment process was "dehumanising" and focused on "what somebody cannot do", rather than "supporting independence".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The government has committed to a recommendation that people receiving end-of-life care or with "serious, well-evidenced conditions" would receive payments without a full assessment.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: It has also agreed to reduce "unnecessary" reviews for people whose conditions are lifelong or unlikely to improve.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Under the report's proposals, cash payments would remain alongside better support to signpost people into education or employment, although claimants could choose to exchange part of their payment for practical services instead.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: In the longer-term, the report recommends changes to the assessment process that look at someone's real-life additional costs and individual needs, focusing on "how people can live the life they want to live, rather than what they cannot do".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: It proposes "improved" questions to understand the extra costs people face, although claimants would not be asked to calculate their costs or provide receipts.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Currently eligibility for Pip is based on how difficult people find carrying out everyday tasks, with two levels of payment available.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: But the review suggests future payment options could include bands more closely linked to extra costs.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The report says its approach is likely to lead to a "rebalancing" of payments, indicating that some claimants could lose out under a new system, either receiving less than they do currently or not qualifying for payments at all.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: "Those with the highest additional costs, and so the most significant needs, should receive the most support," it says.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: "Conversely, this benefit is not appropriate for those who do not incur any additional costs associated with being disabled." The review also calls for an increase in face-to-face assessments, which has been show to reduce eligibility.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The remit of the review was not to produce savings, and it does not set out whether the reforms would reduce the overall welfare bill.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Spending on Pip is set to be about £32bn this financial year, a figure projected to rise to £41.5bn by the end of the decade.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: It comes after a separate review by former minister Alan Milburn into young people not in education, employment or training (Neets).
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The government welcomed Milburn's report , which included a recommendation to move under-25s off Pip and the health element of universal credit, and onto an entirely new benefits system.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: This has led to concerns about a two-tier system, where some people with the same conditions could get different levels of payments depending on their age.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The government has said it will consider the Timms review alongside Milburn's recommendations, with its final proposals set out early next year.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Sir Stephen said this would include detailing the overall costs of changes to the system.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report Eduin Latimer, senior research economist at the Institute for Fiscal Studies think tank, said the review's recommendations had "the potential to better tailor Pip to claimants' needs".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: But he said this would also create challenges, "most importantly in defining what disability-related costs are included, and finding a fair way of measuring them".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Latimer said making it easier to apply for Pip in its current form would "likely increase the number of claimants - and hence spending".
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: However, they have said any changes should not leave disabled people financially worse off.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrats said younger disabled people would now face "months of uncertainty" whilst the government considers the separate reviews from Timms and Milburn, and urged ministers to say quickly what they intend to do.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: The disability benefit system is devolved in Scotland and will not change in line with England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: However, the Timms Review could impact the funding the Scottish government receives.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Disability benefits are also devolved in Northern Ireland, but in practice it reflects any changes made to the system in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Disability benefit review calls for closer link with claimant costs

sentences.text: Rhun ap Iorwerth says the decision shows Westminster is disregarding the views of the people of Wales Wales' First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth has declared he is "gobsmacked" after calls for powers to be handed from Westminster to Cardiff were snubbed.

sentences.text: At the dramatic conclusion of his first party conference speech as Labour leader in September - a moment he has been dreaming of for decades - the prime minister vowed to get closer to the EU.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Over the subsequent two months it has at times been a bit unclear how exactly he envisages that playing out and quite how far he is willing to go.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: But focusing on the process risks obscuring the most important development, which is that the prime minister and the government are now unambiguously committed to Britain not only getting closer, but getting much closer to the EU.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: There were two significant moments at today's summit in that regard.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: First, Burnham said that the government had got as far as it could go with incremental deals with the EU, at least this side of a general election.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: In other words, he has got as far as he believes is possible with the strategy he inherited from Sir Keir Starmer of getting closer to the EU within the confines of the post-Brexit architecture set out by Theresa May all those years ago, of Britain remaining outside the single market and the customs union.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: That suggests that after two years of this, there will not be a third annual summit to unveil specific agreements designed to smooth post-Brexit issues affecting specific sectors.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Yet it does sound like there will be another summit next year - or, rather, an "informal brainstorming process" about potential options for future relations with the EU.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: That sounds pretty nebulous, sure, but an event dedicated specifically to both sides discussing how to change the terms of Britain's arrangements with the EU is likely to become quite a big moment when it arrives.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Perhaps as importantly, von der Leyen made clear that the EU was embracing this event too.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: That said, it does diminish the chances of major movement from Burnham towards embracing a specific model for the EU relationship in the intervening period.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: And what of the domestic politics of this?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Britain's seventh prime minister in just over 10 years watched from Manchester as the fraught relationship with Europe wrecked the careers of so many of those predecessors.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Burnham's gamble is that this time it's different.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: He believes that public regret about how Brexit has played out opens the political space for a far-reaching renegotiation.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Some, especially those who represent Labour's former industrial heartlands, are a little more apprehensive.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: This morning's confusion is a reminder that there is another element to this gamble.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Negotiating with Brussels, even if both sides believe progress is a "win-win", can be a fraught and complicated business.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Once he's on the other side of his brainstorm, can Burnham carry that off without getting bogged down and distracting from his government's other priorities?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: He was talking principally about economic transformation.

sentences.text: From Spring 2027, under 16s will no longer be able to access several social media applications More than 300,000 young people in Britain will work with researchers to help understand how the UK's forthcoming social media ban for under-16s could affect mental health.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: The studies will examine the habits of the children and teenagers, including whether they spend less time on their phones and what they are replacing scrolling with.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Ten different projects have been commissioned, taking place across England, Wales and Scotland, to help reflect a diverse range of teenagers.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: The social media ban, beginning in spring 2027, will follow a similar model to that already introduced in Australia to stop children accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Apps such as Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Snapchat and YouTube will be banned under new rules The work, funded by health charity The Wellcome Trust, will help inform future online safety policies in the UK and internationally, with some early results available before the ban happens.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Researchers will use wearable technology, smartphones, digital diaries and surveys to collect data to see how young people respond to the ban, both physically and mentally.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: And they will check whether young people find ways to circumvent restrictions.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Dr Camilla Iannone, research lead at Wellcome, said it was a once-in-a-generation opportunity to study at scale how social media and its restrictions affected youth mental health.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: "We really don't think that this is a simple binary question of whether social media is good or bad, or whether restrictions work or don't work.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: "Instead, the teams will study whether changing young people's digital environment leads to meaningful changes in their mental health and wellbeing." Participants are being recruited to reflect a diverse range of young people, including different genders and sexual orientations.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: People with existing mental health conditions, such as anxiety and depression, will also be included, as well as young people who are neurodivergent.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Groups have been set up at Cardiff University, the University of Oxford, the University of Birmingham, King's College London, the University of Edinburgh, the University of Manchester, the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, and University College London.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Online forum Reddit and a digital rights group are currently involved in a high court battle in the country, arguing that the law change is unconstitutional.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: There have also been reports of Australian teens finding ways to get round the ban - with the UK government promising to make sure tougher blocks are in place.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health
