sentences.text: Sabrina Bahsoon now has more than 900,000 followers across social media Sabrina Bahsoon became known globally as Tube Girl after self-shot videos of her dancing and lip-syncing on the London Underground blew up online.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: The 26-year-old content creator had the world at her feet when she went viral in 2023 , going on to build a social media following of more than 900,000 people.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She signed major brand endorsement deals and was pursuing a music career.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: But then her "whole life turned upside down" when she had what appeared to be a psychotic episode.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Her symptoms made her violent and erratic, leading to her being sectioned in a mental health hospital - where doctors treated her with anti-psychotic medication.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: But Bahsoon's family, helped by her father's neurologist friend, pushed for further tests.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: And two months into her hospital treatment, doctors got to the truth.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Sabrina Bahsoon shot to fame for her viral Tube videos but in March 2026 her life turned upside down overnight.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She actually had a rare, but treatable, autoimmune disease which is known to sometimes present as psychiatric symptoms, as well as seizures, confusion and memory loss.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: In her first interview since the experience, she tells BBC News she wants hospitals to offer a series of tests as standard practice if patients have these symptoms.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "In a way I do feel let down by the care I received.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: I feel like the urgency to discover what was actually wrong with me wasn't there," she says.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "And I also feel as a woman being written off completely as a psychotic patient without further investigation was a mistake." A spokesperson for the hospital she attended has apologised for Bahsoon's experience and says an investigation has been launched into her care.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: The content creator was in hospital for about four months earlier this year Bahsoon first had "psychotic symptoms" in March this year after filming a video on the Tube with girl group Flo.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She says that evening she began to scream, cry and her conversations became "very erratic".
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: The next day she broke up with her boyfriend, which prompted her sisters to check on her, as it was so unexpected.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Bahsoon says her condition got worse, becoming violent towards herself and posting videos which didn't make sense, before her sisters called 999 for an ambulance.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "I'm normally a very relaxed person, maybe anxious at times, but the way I was speaking about harming myself and the way I was screaming and being violent was super out of character for me," she says.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: A&E doctors initially thought her symptoms could have been provoked by stress and a lack of sleep, discharging her with sleeping tablets.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She then began destroying things at home and spoke about having hallucinations, which led to police bringing her to hospital in handcuffs.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Bahsoon was sectioned and moved to a psychiatric ward where she was treated with antipsychotic medication, which she says made her "docile".
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "I went from being a total firecracker to being completely catatonic," she says.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "I stopped eating, drinking.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: I could not speak properly." Bahsoon has "very faint memories" of this period, she says, but her family has since shown her clips of her having breakdowns which she finds "heartbreaking".
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Sabrina Bahsoon was pursuing a music career at the height of her fame After two months on the psychiatric ward, Bahsoon was diagnosed with an autoimmune disease called anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: It was caused by tumours in her ovaries, known as teratomas, producing antibodies which attacked her body.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She had surgery to remove the tumours in June, which she says brought on a "drastic" change in her behaviour from "freaking out" to having more understanding of what was happening around her.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Bahsoon has since been recovering back in her home country of Malaysia and is having therapy to "deal with all the trauma".
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: But she says she feels "very lucky" as doctors have told her she is part of a small percentage of people who they expect to make a full recovery.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: The content creator first revealed what happened in a TikTok video in October, and says she is sharing her story as she wants to raise awareness of the disease.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She also wants to "push people to advocate for themselves" if they feel they're not getting the "treatment they deserve".
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "I do want reform in the way that hospitals deal with psychotic patients or patients that present with psychotic symptoms," she says.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "I hope I'm sharing my story so that nobody else has to go through this." She plans to return to her content creation in the new year and is looking forward to "enjoying life with a whole new perspective and appreciation for what I do and what I now can help people with".
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis is more typical in women and mainly affects young people, with about 40% of cases aged under 18, according to the charity Encephalitis International (EI) , external .
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Dr Ava Easton MBE, chief executive of EI, says a "frightening" aspect is how quickly someone's behaviour and personality can appear to change.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "A person may suddenly seem confused, distressed or [to be] experiencing psychosis when the underlying problem is actually inflammation of their brain," she says.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: She says there's a "real risk" of it going undiagnosed and encourages people to look out for the warning signs , external .
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: According to the NHS , external , cases of all types of encephalitis are rare, and EI says the condition affects about 6,000 people in the UK each year.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: A spokesperson for Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, which was the first to treat Bahsoon, said they were "very sorry" for what she experienced.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: They said an internal review found some aspects of her initial assessment "were not followed up as they should have been" and an investigation had been started.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: Dr Ed Beveridge, divisional medical director at Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust, also confirmed they'd be part of that review.
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: He said anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis was a "rare autoimmune condition" that is not "routinely screened for nationally".
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: "We are pleased that her condition has now been identified and treated." If you have been affected by the issues raised in this article, help and support is available via BBC Action Line .
sentences.article_title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis

sentences.text: US rapper Don Toliver has postponed two shows in London this week, after his concert in Manchester on Sunday was evacuated when an "unknown substance" was released into the crowd.
sentences.article_title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation

sentences.text: Toliver was due to play The O2 on Monday and Wembley Arena on Tuesday, but  Live Nation said his "stage and production equipment remains in Manchester and cannot be moved in time".
sentences.article_title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation

sentences.text: One person was taken to hospital and 89 people showed "symptoms believed to be linked to the exposure" after Sunday's Co-op Live arena show, police said.
sentences.article_title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation

sentences.text: Fans described "distressing scenes" with people "choking", "screaming" and "coughing up blood" because of the effects of a substance, which police initially believed to be tear gas.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Coughs, confusion and boos as Co-op Live concert cancelled The Wembley show has been rescheduled to 14 December, while Monday night's O2 gig has been moved to 15 December.
sentences.article_title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation

sentences.text: "I'm very sad to sit here and say I have to reschedule The O2 London show to December 15th due to (the) unfortunate incident last night," Don Toliver wrote on Instagram.

sentences.text: Greater Manchester Police (GMP) declared a major incident on Sunday and said 12,000 people were evacuated from the arena.
sentences.article_title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation

sentences.text: One woman was taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further assessment and treatment after the incident, which happened at about 22:00 GMT, the force said.
sentences.article_title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation

sentences.text: A further 88 people "underwent dry decontamination at the scene and were subsequently accommodated within the Etihad Stadium while the incident was managed", according to GMP.

sentences.article_title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation

sentences.text: "It just hit me in the throat," he said, adding that it felt like "burning".
sentences.article_title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation

sentences.text: There was "a bit of panic", Douzi said: "Everybody was having the same feeling and trying to get out." Some fans reported eye and respiratory symptoms, according to the North West Ambulance Service.

Police launched an investigation and are continuing to carry out tests on items at the venue to try to identify the substance.

sentences.text: No arrests have been made.
sentences.article_title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation

sentences.text: Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said: "Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk.
sentences.article_title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation

sentences.text: Testing will take place throughout the day as the investigation into the cause of this incident progresses.

sentences.text: "We are trying to establish whether any criminality has occurred in relation to this incident." Some fans complained about security and a lack of searches as people went into the Manchester concert.

sentences.article_title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation

sentences.text: Now, with Manchester United making their worst start to a league season since 1972, it raises the question: are United this season's Spurs?

sentences.text: While Tottenham finished 17th with just 41 points last term, they actually started the season better than United have this season.

sentences.text: After 11 games in 2025-26, Spurs were riding high in fifth with 18 points - 10 more than United have now.

sentences.text: United's expected goal difference is almost identical to Tottenham's at this stage last season, but this time the table is more honest, even if United are perhaps not as bad as it makes out.

sentences.article_title: Are Man Utd this season's Tottenham?

sentences.article_title: Are Man Utd this season's Tottenham?

sentences.article_title: Are Man Utd this season's Tottenham?

sentences.text: United are converting just 7% of their chances and conceding 16% of their opponents' - a poor combination for any team.

sentences.text: Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife Carla Bruni-Sarkozy are to face trial next year over charges stemming from the former French president's conviction for conspiring to fund his election campaign with money from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi.
sentences.article_title: French ex-President Sarkozy and wife Carla Bruni to face trial

sentences.text: The charges centre on the retraction of the testimony of a key witness who had initially said he had evidence that could incriminate Sarkozy.
sentences.article_title: French ex-President Sarkozy and wife Carla Bruni to face trial

sentences.text: The pair deny any wrongdoing.
sentences.article_title: French ex-President Sarkozy and wife Carla Bruni to face trial

sentences.text: Sarkozy was given a five-year sentence in the case last September and became the first French ex-president to go to jail, even though he only spent 20 days behind bars.

sentences.text: He has always denied doing anything wrong in the case and the appeals verdict is expected next Monday.

sentences.article_title: French ex-President Sarkozy and wife Carla Bruni to face trial

sentences.article_title: French ex-President Sarkozy and wife Carla Bruni to face trial

sentences.text: Pope Francis claimed he saw the devil three times over the course of his life, as well as the "gates of hell", according to new extracts from his private diary.
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: In The Private Diary of Pope Francis, published on Tuesday, a 2021 entry lists the late pontiff as having three visions of the devil: once from a car, another "in the choir loft" during Mass, and a third during a meeting with Vatican officials.
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: "I can't forget the powerful raspiness of his voice," Francis wrote, recalling one of the visions.
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: In the diary, written from 1992 to 2024, he also expresses regret over his 2018 visit to Chile, when he was criticised for defending a bishop who was accused of covering up sexual abuse committed by a priest.
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: Francis, who led the Catholic Church for 12 years until his death in 2025, later apologised and summoned the country's bishops to Rome, where they all offered to resign .
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: "Devastated because of the situation in Chile," Francis wrote in a 2021 entry.
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: "It was hard for me to admit what happened in Chile; I didn't think it was so serious." Of his encounters, which Francis interpreted as meetings with the devil, he said he could not forget the devil's "menacing" eyes.
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: "He looked at me with flaming eyes... more intense than the previous one.
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: They were like flashes of fire," he wrote of his second vision that he said happened inside a Carmelite chapel while he was archbishop of Buenos Aires.
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: He said the devil's presence intruded on his journeys, including during the visit to Chile amid the clerical sexual abuse scandal, and a meeting a few days after he had returned to Rome.
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: "I saw him and heard his voice, triumphant, possessing everything," he wrote, adding that "the Lord gave me the chance to free myself from these encounters".
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: The collection of diaries was edited by a longtime friend of Francis The late pope also revealed that while getting ready to go to sleep in June 2018, he "saw the gates of hell".
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: "I watched a little, and it terrified me," he said, adding that he "took the rosary as a weapon".
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: "It's dangerous to get close to the gates of hell, because flames can spring out and burn," he wrote.
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: Cardinal Victor Fernandez, head of the Vatican's Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith and friend of Francis, edited the diaries, which are the first by a pope to be released to the public since the 1960s.
sentences.article_title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

sentences.text: Nato chief Mark Rutte and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz respond to reports of Russian plans to launch nuclear weapons into space Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after German reports that Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media.
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: It was not clear which country had authored the reports.
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said such reports were "not new, yet they remain no less shocking", and a government spokesman said the reports were being taken "very seriously".
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he had not seen the reports but dismissed stories citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously".
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: The Russian embassy in Berlin told German media it rejected what it called "unfounded allegations" and said the reports were part of a "propaganda campaign".
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: Citing anonymous German military and intelligence sources, public broadcasters NDR and WDR and newspaper Süddeutscher Zeitung, said the Russian satellite was dubbed "Sputnik-S" and was equipped with a nuclear warhead.
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: It could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites, including important communication and observation satellites.
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: "When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary." Merz did not confirm or deny the reports of Russia's plans, but said they "reveal the level of escalation Russia is evidently prepared to pursue".
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: German government spokesman Stefan Kornelius warned against causing "excessive nervousness regarding hypothetical dangers".
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: Josef Aschbacher, the head of the European Space Agency, told the Handeslblatt newspaper that having nuclear weapons in space was "the ultimate nightmare scenario".
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: Russia is a signatory to the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which bans weapons of mass destruction from orbit.
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: Bleddyn Bowen, co-director of the Space Research Centre at Durham University, said that exploding a nuclear weapon in space would have "massive infrastructural effects" as there were now more than 15,000 active satellites.
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: But he told the BBC's Today programme that "the effect of these weapons would be extremely indiscriminate and also take out a lot of Russia's own space infrastructure".
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: Other countries, including the US and China, have deployed or plan to deploy other weapons in space, exploring other capabilities outside of the treaty, such as targeting rivals' satellites - which are key for military communications, surveillance and navigation.
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: In 2024 the US accused Russia of developing a "space-based" anti-satellite weapon armed with a nuclear warhead.
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: Russia denied the accusation .
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: "Our position is clear and transparent.
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: We have always been categorically against the deployment of nuclear weapons in space and we are still against it," President Vladimir Putin said at the time.
sentences.article_title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports

sentences.text: Gisèle Pelicot said she would take legal action against the publisher and author of the essay Gisèle Pelicot has said she has been "once again humiliated" after nude images of her were sent to the media to promote a book about coercive control.
sentences.article_title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book

sentences.text: The 73-year-old told French broadcaster BFM TV she would take legal action against the publisher and author of the essay.
sentences.article_title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book

sentences.text: Pelicot made headlines across the world when she waived her right to anonymity in the trial of her then-husband Dominique, who was jailed for 20 years for drugging and raping her, as well as allowing other men to rape her while she was unconscious.
sentences.article_title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book

sentences.text: The publisher apologised, saying it would no longer print or promote the work after "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication".
sentences.article_title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book

sentences.text: Pelicot told BFM: "I am deeply shocked that images from the most intimate part of my private life are being displayed and exploited for commercial purposes." "Today I find myself once again humiliated, exposed and hurt, as if the ordeal of the trial had not been enough," she said.
sentences.article_title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book

sentences.text: The essay was written by Sabine Prokhoris, a philosopher and psychoanalyst, who has previously criticised the Me Too movement.
sentences.article_title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book

sentences.text: French media reported that Tinbad, a small Paris publishing house, emailed nude photos of Pelicot taken by her ex-husband to some media outlets in order to promote the essay.

sentences.text: In a statement on its website, Tinbad said that no further print runs of the book would be produced beyond the 280 copies already in circulation.

sentences.text: "We offer our sincerest apologies to Ms Gisèle Pelicot," it said.
sentences.article_title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book

sentences.text: The company also apologised to the author.
sentences.article_title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book

sentences.text: Tinbad said "no images of rape or pornographic videos" were sent to the media.
sentences.article_title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book

sentences.text: "These psychological situations, fundamentally ambiguous in nature, involve each of the parties in an equally responsible, though not symmetrical, way," it said.

sentences.article_title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book

sentences.article_title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book

sentences.text: Shark Tank investor Kevin O'Leary is behind a major AI data centre project in Canada that has so far been embraced by legislators.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: As Americans have grown increasingly sour on artificial intelligence (AI) data centre development, Canada's industry leaders are sensing an opportunity.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "Data centres in Canada looking pretty appealing right now," Lucy Hargreaves, CEO of non-profit policy group Build Canada, wrote on X the day after American voters passed 40 of 41 local ballot initiatives aimed at limiting or preventing data centre development in this month's midterm elections.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: While the number of proposed AI data centres in the US dwarfs that of its northern neighbour, in recent months Canada is being increasingly pitched as a hub for these so-called "hyperscale" projects.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Those in favour argue that Canada's abundant land, natural gas and cold climate make it uniquely positioned to address some of the problems facing US AI infrastructure, from data centres' proximity to populated areas to noise pollution and strain on electricity grids.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "Some of the capital that would have been deployed to build data centres in the US is now more available for Canada," Hargreaves told the BBC in an interview.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "The question really is whether or not we want to go for that." Unlike in the US, pushback to these projects in Canada has been muted - at least so far.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Many are going ahead without significant disruptions, and legislators have openly embraced them without major political consequences.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: At the heart of Canada's AI data centre boom is Alberta, where 90% of all currently proposed sites are set to be built.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The western Canadian province, rich with natural gas deposits, has pitched itself as "North America's destination of choice" for AI data centres, including by offering a "concierge" service for investors to help build these projects at "unparalleled speed".
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: One of those investors is Kevin O'Leary, the Canadian businessman, TV personality and an ally of Donald Trump, who announced plans this year to build two large AI data centres - one in Alberta and one in the US state of Utah.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: His planned sites, both named Wonder Valley, are being received in very different ways on either side of the border.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Residents in Utah have organised a fierce opposition campaign. , external The pushback led outgoing state senator Stuart Adams to demand in June that O'Leary scale down the project by 75% , external , from 40,000 to 13,000 acres.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Financing for the Utah Wonder Valley data centre is still underway, and it is unclear when - and if - shovels will hit the ground on the project.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The proposed 7,000-acre, 7.5-gigawatt Alberta Wonder Valley project, meanwhile, has received strong backing from both the provincial government and the local municipality.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The project is billed as "off-grid" , external , relying on its own power system fuelled by natural gas sourced from the region.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: In April, the Alberta government exempted the project from an environmental impact assessment , external , arguing it was unnecessary, though it will still need to obtain permits prior to construction.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The project was met with only limited opposition at a local town hall earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: One resident, Dan Harms, told Bloomberg in June , external that he saw the economic benefits of the Wonder Valley data centre and that it was being built "out in the middle of nowhere".
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: In an interview with BBC News, Reeve Ryan Ratzlaf, of Greenview Municipality in north-western Alberta, said the project was the "perfect fit" for his rural community, which had been looking for an industrial tenant to fill a resource-rich parcel of land for 13 years.

sentences.text: Some community members have expressed concern about the amount of water needed to cool the proposed site annually, which is projected to be six million cubic metres, or about the size of 2,400 Olympic-size swimming pools.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Ratzlaf argued the amount was a drop compared to the annual flow of the nearby Smoky River, from which the centre would pull water.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: More broadly, he said he believed that economic benefits to the region outweighed potential risks.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "It's a giant warehouse with computer equipment inside," he said, arguing that it was less risky than petrochemical plants that could have been built in its place.
